energy_provenance.hardware_class: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Zen 5, 32 logical CPUs, Linux x86_64)

counters.core_reported_j: /sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:0:0/energy_uj (core domain MSR_CORE_ENERGY_STAT, process and children pinned to domain lead CPU 0 via sched_setaffinity)

energy_provenance.primary_energy_metric: core_reported_j (median across M=5 independent batch trials on pinned CPU 0; package_reported_j and paired local-sleep-subtracted core_net_reported_j logged alongside)

E4_Energy.objective: Measure compilation energy E_compile (reported_j), wall time, artifact byte length |bin|, per-invocation execution energy E_run (reported_j), and empirical optimization payback horizon N* = ceil(Delta E_compile / Delta E_run) across 20 deterministic integer/fixed-point kernels in C, Rust, WebAssembly, Python, and RCE; additionally evaluate H4 Regime-B variance explained (bootstrap adjusted R^2 over 2,000 whole-kernel resamples).
compiler_tiers: rce check + 5-target emit (core, rust, python, js, scala) -> node js
rce check + emit rust -> rustc -C opt-level=3
E4_Energy.equivalence_gate: Exact 64-bit unsigned batch checksum equality across all compiler tiers and languages for every kernel over identical seed ranges; any mismatch voids the cell.
E4_Energy.payback_horizon_formula: N* = 0 if Delta E_compile <= 0 and Delta E_run > 0; ceil(Delta E_compile / Delta E_run) if Delta E_compile > 0 and Delta E_run > 0; infinity ('never') if Delta E_run <= 0.
E4_Energy.h4_regime_b_analysis: Across Clang and Rust optimization tiers with WebAssembly IR description length lambda (ir_nodes, wasm_bytes) and dynamic instruction count, compute OLS adjusted R^2 for (dynamic_ops + lambda) vs Regime-B baseline (wall_s * mean_power_w) with 2,000 whole-kernel bootstrap resamples.

E5_Scale.objective: Test name-free De Bruijn / positional reuse hashing (H5) at >10x scale across all 185 emitted Forms of the W1 RCE corpus plus 60 C/Rust/Python kernel programs (245 base programs) under equivalence-preserving renamings/formatting/declaration shifts and 500 test-vector-verified non-equivalent semantic mutations, and measure avoided compilation reported_j.

hypotheses_and_falsifiers.H5_Scale_Support: debruijn_nameless_sha256 achieves strictly higher hit rate on alpha-renamed pairs than raw_sha256 and ws_comment_strip_sha256 across both the 185 W1 Forms and the 60 C/Rust/Python kernels, AND achieves 0 / 500 (0.00%) false-positive hash collisions on verified semantic mutants.
hypotheses_and_falsifiers.H5_Scale_Falsifier: Any false-positive collision (> 0 / 500) on debruijn_nameless_sha256, or no hit-rate gain over raw/whitespace-stripped hashes on alpha-renamed pairs.
hypotheses_and_falsifiers.Binding_Swap_Contrast: naive_ast_token_kind_sha256 (identifier-stripping without De Bruijn binding indices) is predicted to suffer false-positive collisions on binding-swap mutants (e.g. x - y -> y - x), demonstrating empirically why De Bruijn positional binding indices are necessary for soundness.

E5_Scale.cache_energy_measurement: Measure RAPL core_reported_j and package_reported_j of cold compilation vs warm De Bruijn nameless hash cache hit across rce check + 5-target emit, clang -O3, and rustc -C opt-level=3.
